cards.front: What should you know about key distinction?
cards.back: System software manages the computer and provides a platform for other software. Application software performs tasks for the user. System software works behind the scenes; application software is what the user interacts with directly.

cards.front: Recall a key point about Software Classification
cards.back: An operating system (OS) is system software that manages computer hardware and software resources. It provides common services for application programs and acts as an intermediary between the user and the hardware.

cards.front: Recall a key point about Software Classification
cards.back: Utility programs are system software that perform maintenance and housekeeping tasks to keep the computer running efficiently. They are not essential for the computer to function but help maintain performance and security.

cards.front: Recall a key point about Software Classification
cards.back: Defragmentation is only needed for HDD (magnetic disk drives). SSDs do not need defragmentation because they have no moving parts and can access any location instantly. In fact, defragmenting an SSD can reduce its lifespan.

cards.front: Recall a key point about Software Classification
cards.back: Backups should be stored in a different location from the original data (offsite or in the cloud). This protects against physical disasters (fire, flood, theft) that could destroy both the original and the backup if stored together.

cards.front: What should you know about gcse computer science exam tips?
cards.back: System software: OS, utilities, translators, libraries. Application software: user tasks. Compiler: all at once, fast execution, hides source. Interpreter: line by line, slower execution, easier debugging. Assembler: translates assembly language to machine code. Open source ≠ free. Know examples of each software type. For comparison questions, give equal detail on both sides.
Manage hardware and provide a platform (e.g. Perform specific tasks for the user)
Often runs in background (e.g. User interacts directly)
Runs without application software (e.g. Cannot run without system software)
OS, drivers, utilities, translators (e.g. Word processor, browser, games)
Essential for computer to function (e.g. Optional - installed as needed)
Fragments scattered across disk (e.g. File pieces stored together)
Slow - read head moves frequently (e.g. Fast - read head moves less)
More movement = more wear (e.g. Less movement = less wear)
